items.originalTitle: Dem govs huddle to address living costs
items.author: Samuel Benson and Erin Doherty
items.title: Dem govs huddle to address living costs
items.summary: PARK CITY, Utah — Cost-of-living concerns fueled Democrats to victory this month. Now they’re preparing to do something about it. As newly elected governors gathered for a job training conference hosted by the National Governors Association, conversations among the Democrat-heavy group often turned to the economic woes in their states — and the necessity to get something done quickly. “What are the things that we can do — not in the first 100 days, but in the first 100 hours — that can start bringing some relief to the American people?” Wes Moore, the National Governors Association chair and Maryland governor, said in an interview with POLITICO. Health care and home costs topped the target list. Several newly elected Democratic governors — Jocelyn Benson in Michigan, Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, Deb Haaland in New Mexico and Rob Sand in Iowa — plan to take action to lower health costs, ranging from caps on prescription drug prices to expanding Medicaid coverage, within days of taking office. California Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra promised to spur affordable housing construction. His Nevada counterpart, Aaron Ford, said he plans to limit corporations purchasing private homes, and is preparing a day-one executive order to task every state agency with “finding ways to put money back in people's pockets.” “You hear people signing executive orders to make things easier for businesses, cut regulations, and make it easier to do business. I think that's cool, that's fine, that's dandy,” Ford said in an interview. “But if you can do it for businesses, you can do it for people, too.” Affordability was, far and away, the top issue for voters this cycle. Results from The POLITICO Poll, conducted just days after the midterm elections, found a 47% plurality of Americans — including 59% of Democratic voters and 41% of Republicans — said affordability and the economy were among the main issues driving their vote. Democrats’ tsunami washed over governors’ mansions across the nation: They won 24 of the 36 governor’s races held this month, flipping red states like Texas, Alaska and Ohio, and will hold 30 of the 50 governorships nationwide next year — the most in three decades. These governors and soon-to-be governors will be buoyed by a boon of Democrats in their statehouses: Democrats won unified control of government in Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada and Wisconsin; in North Carolina, Democrats flipped the House for the first time in 16 years and broke Republicans’ supermajority in the Senate. As several inches of snow descended on the Wasatch Front and blanketed the glitzy ski resort in Park City this week, the newly elected governors sheltered inside the NGA’s New Governors Leadership Forum — colloquially called “baby governors’ school.” At the two-day seminar, the incoming state executives and their teams attended seminars and workshops, mingled over hors d'oeuvres and heard from current and former governors on what to expect. Former President Bill Clinton, sitting spread-legged in a Team USA sweater Thursday, dished to a room full of governors on his book recommendations (“The Social Conquest of Earth” by E.O. Wilson), fun facts (“The combined weight of ants on earth exceeds the combined weight of all the people on earth!”) and political predictions (“I think if President Trump gets closer to leaving, he may get more interested in leaving actual legacies in forms other than buildings.”) Clinton, who chaired the NGA when he served as governor of Arkansas, also offered some advice to the newly electeds: “The most important thing is that you and your Cabinet and your office and your organizations out in the state know what your priorities are and know what your progress is.” Governors will face a steep climb to deliver immediate relief to Americans. Economic forces are national and international, and much of the past year’s price spikes, from fuel to food to energy, can be tied to the Iran war. Bottoms said she will immediately begin to prepare Georgia agencies for Medicaid expansion, and expects the state legislature — with Democrats now in control of the state House, while Republicans still control the state Senate — to cooperate. “I do believe this is an issue we will get bipartisan support on,” she told POLITICO. In addition to his Day-One executive order, Ford says he plans to work with the Nevada legislature to sign bills in his first 30 days on expanding free public school meals, lowering the cost of prescription drugs to the Medicaid negotiated price and limiting corporations’ ability to buy private homes. Benson said she has already reached out to the Trump administration about tariffs, which includes a 50% tariff on most Canadian exports and have disproportionately impacted Michiganders. She said she has not yet heard back, but “the point is I have reached out, and I do hope to have that conversation.” She also emphasized her focus on lowering health care costs. “That's life or death for so many families,” Benson said. Megan Messerly and Adam Wren contributed reporting.

These viruses can significantly impact microbiome processes, not only by killing their host but also sometimes by temporarily providing additional capabilities to their host. As many viruses have not been grown in a lab, connecting them to their natural hosts has been difficult. A new bioinformatics toolkit and database are now available to help researchers make those associations at an unprecedented scale.

items.originalTitle: Multiplying your Switch 2’s storage costs less than usual right now
items.author: Cameron Faulkner
items.title: Multiplying your Switch 2’s storage costs less than usual right now
items.summary: Expanding your Nintendo Switch 2’s 256GB of built-in storage with a microSD card is pricier than it was with Nintendo’s original console. That’s because microSD Express cards , while physically identical to ones you might have lying around, have faster read and write speeds. Thankfully, Samsung’s 256GB model has dropped to $44.99 at Amazon ahead of Black Friday, which is a few bucks off its usual price but still well below its $79.99 MSRP. Sandisk’s 256GB card, meanwhile, is available for $49.99 ($10 off Amazon’s typical list price) from Amazon and Sandisk , if you prefer one brand over the other for some reason. For those who don’t want to think about upgrading their Switch 2’s storage again, both brands’ 512GB microSD Express cards are selling for a fair $99.99 on Amazon . That gives you double the storage for roughly twice the price of a 256GB card, as it should be. Samsung P9 microSD Express Card Where to Buy: $79.99 $44.99 at Amazon (256GB) $149.99 $99.99 at Amazon (512GB) Sandisk microSD Express card Where to Buy: $166.99 $99.99 at Best Buy (512GB) $73.99 $49.99 at Amazon (256GB) $166.99 $98.99 at Amazon (512GB) I suspect the 256GB option will be enough for most Switch 2 players, unless you buy a lot of games. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is 24.9 gigabytes, for example. Other Nintendo-developed games tend to be similar in install size, though it’s all over the place for third-party game makers; Resident Evil Requiem (which also recently dropped to $39.99 on Amazon ) is relatively small at 28.7 gigs, while The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered is about 50. Some games take up even more storage.

items.originalTitle: Here are the Apple deals actually worth picking up ahead of Black Friday

items.title: Here are the Apple deals actually worth picking up ahead of Black Friday
items.summary: A new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch can make a great holiday gift, but they can also take a pretty big dent out of your budget. That’s especially true this year, as rising hardware prices have made MacBooks and other Apple devices even more expensive. Fortunately, Black Friday offers a chance to save, especially since great deals are already available on a wide range of Apple devices. Some discounts even extend to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro , which have dropped to new lows. Most of the discounts below are promoted as Black Friday deals, but we’ve also included a few that aren’t technically part of the shopping event but have “coincidentally” dropped in price in the last week or so. Black Friday isn’t until November 27th, however, so some prices could fall further in the coming days. Apple is also kicking off its own Black Friday shopping event that day, offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases. That said, if you don’t want to wait, we think the deals below are already worth taking advantage of. Earbud and headphone deals AirPods Pro 3 The latest AirPods Pro offer improved noise cancellation and richer bass, along with built-in heart sensors that work with Apple’s Fitness app to monitor calories burned across more than 50 workouts. Read our review. Where to Buy: $249 $179 at Amazon $249 $179 at Walmart $249 $179.99 at Best Buy Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 Beats’ fitness-focused earbuds feature ear hooks designed to stay put during even the most intense workouts as well as built-in heart rate monitoring. They also deliver relatively bass-rich sound for their design, along with solid noise cancellation, wireless charging, and AirPods features like adaptive audio thanks to Apple’s H2 chip. Read our review. Where to Buy: $249 $179.95 at Amazon $249 $179.95 at Walmart $249.99 $179.99 at Best Buy You can buy the AirPods 4 on sale at Walmart for around $89 ($40 off), which is $20 shy of their best price. They also offer voice call quality on par with the latest AirPods Pro. Read our review . The second-gen AirPods Max are down to $419 ($130 off) at Amazon , which is $19 shy of their best price to date ( Best Buy and Target also have them for about $10 more). Like the original, Apple’s latest over-ear headphones feature a luxurious build consisting of aluminum, steel, and a mesh fabric, but they offer better sound and noise cancellation. The new H2 chip also enables features like adaptive audio and live translation. Read our review . Beats Studio Pro The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review . Where to Buy: $349.99 $139.95 at Amazon $349.99 $149 at Walmart $349.99 $149.95 at Best Buy Beats 360 headphones The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. It’s also noticeably thinner and lighter than the non-touchscreen 16-inch MacBook Pro, and features a new Dynamic Island that replaces the notch and provides quick access to controls and notifications.
